alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 27 at 3:52PM EDT until September 28 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Up to one to two feet of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways with compromised dune structures.

* WHERE...Areas along the beaches, Pamlico Sound, and adjacent
tidal creeks.

* WHEN...Until midnight EDT tonight.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways with compromised dune structures resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Portions of Highway 12 remain
closed between Pony Pens and the ferry dock. Low lying
property including homes, businesses, and some critical
infrastructure may still be inundated. Some roads and low
lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes
adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides on Sunday are around 8:40 PM.
alerts.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
alerts.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island

alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 27 at 3:52PM EDT until September 28 at 12:00AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways with compromised dune structures. Elevated
water levels due to high astronomical tides and moderate west
winds may lead to localized minor flooding of low-lying areas
prone to soundside flooding. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves, and hazardous
debris expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks ocean-side locales that
experienced weakening of dune structures over the last few
days. For soundside localized flooding, low-lying areas prone
to sound- side flooding in and near Manteo.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until midnight EDT
tonight. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways with compromised dune structures resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Dangerous swimming and surfing
conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The next oceanside high tide times are
around 8:30 PM Sunday. The soundside high times are around
11:30 AM Sunday and midnight Sunday night. The most likely
time for strong rip currents to occur is a couple hours either
side of low tide, which will occur around 2:30 PM Sunday.
alerts.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Watch out for debris that may be in the water.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 27 at 12:29PM MST until September 29 at 9:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Arizona, including the following
areas, Aguila Valley, Apache Junction/Gold Canyon, Cave Creek/New
River, Deer Valley, Dripping Springs, Fountain Hills/East Mesa,
Globe/Miami, Mazatzal Mountains, New River Mesa, Northwest Valley,
Pinal/Superstition Mountains, Rio Verde/Salt River, San Carlos,
Southeast Gila County, Superior and Tonto Basin.

* WHEN...From late Monday night through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The combination of deep tropical moisture moving into the area
from the south and an approaching weather disturbance from the
west will result in showers and thunderstorms capable of
producing localized heavy rainfall. Moderate to heavy rainfall
rates in excess of 1-2 inches per hour are expected. Some areas
will see training of storms leading to heavier rainfall
accumulations.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
alerts.areaDesc: Aguila Valley; Northwest Valley; Cave Creek/New River; Deer Valley; New River Mesa; Rio Verde/Salt River; Fountain Hills/East Mesa; Superior; Apache Junction/Gold Canyon; Tonto Basin; Mazatzal Mountains; Pinal/Superstition Mountains; San Carlos; Dripping Springs; Globe/Miami; Southeast Gila County

alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 27 at 12:18PM PDT until September 29 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. For the High
Surf Advisory, breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with dangerous
rip currents.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Focused
across exposed south facing coasts.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through 5 AM Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory and High Surf Advisory, from 5
AM Monday to 5 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to locally significant beach
erosion is likely. Very localized damage possible to most
vulnerable areas. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to
sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of most concern are Avalon, Long
Beach (Peninsula and Belmont Shore). While the surf will likely
be smaller than Marie (from earlier this month), the lingering
erosion effects enhance the vulnerabilities for locally more
significant coastal flooding.
alerts.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
alerts.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

alerts.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued September 27 at 12:18PM PDT until September 30 at 4:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves of 3 to 5
feet. Minor tidal overflows possible, especially Monday and
Tuesday.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Pooling of sea water is possible around high tide
at beach and harbor areas (including Santa Barbara Harbor).
Enhanced beach erosion is also possible. No significant damage
is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Locally moderate coastal flooding impacts
possible but unlikely for areas such as Santa Barbara Harbor.
These impacts may include moderate flooding of sea water over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Additionally, locally moderate
beach erosion is possible.
alerts.instruction:

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

alerts.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 27 at 1:01PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
ESFGJT

Strong southwesterly winds ahead of a closed low centered over
California will pull tropical moisture from Tropical Storm Odalys and
Hurricane Polo towards eastern Utah and western Colorado, with
atmospheric moisture peaking in our area on Monday. The northerly
extent of the expected excessive rainfall poses a threat to our
southern San Juan river basins. Current forecasts suggest 1 to 4
inches of rain Monday morning through early Wednesday. At face value,
rivers and tributaries will see a rise due to the forecast rainfall.
However, localized heavier amounts could result in flooding across
the southern San Juan foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been recently observed.
However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts (i.e. above 90th
percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action stage to minor
flooding. Most probable basins to see significant rises include; the
Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito Creek, and the
Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Confidence has increased enough for a Flood Watch to be issued
for southern portions of the forecast area valid from 6am Monday
through 6am Wednesday. Continue to monitor the latest forecasts
especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in the Watch
areas.

possible.

* WHERE...Southern New Mexico and Far West Texas.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

Hurricane Polo Monday and Tuesday, bringing widespread showers

repeated rounds of rain may result in scattered instances of
flash flooding. Heavy rainfall from last week has saturated soils

alerts.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 27 at 2:29PM EDT until September 28 at 3:00AM EDT by NWS Gray ME
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
with up to 1 foot of inundation and large breaking waves
leading to splash over and beach erosion. This is a long
duration event... with these impacts felt over multiple tide
cycles continuing through this evening, possibly through the
Monday daytime high tide. For the High Surf Advisory, large
breaking waves of 7 to 12 feet and a high risk of rip currents.

* WHERE...In Maine, Coastal York County. In New Hampshire,
Coastal Rockingham County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 AM EDT Monday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.
alerts.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.
alerts.areaDesc: Coastal York; Coastal Rockingham

alerts.description:

possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, east central, north central,
northeast, and southeast New Mexico, including the following areas,
in central New Mexico, Central Highlands, Eastern Lincoln County
and Estancia Valley. In east central New Mexico, Curry County, De
Baca County, Guadalupe County, Quay County and Roosevelt County. In
north central New Mexico, East Slopes Sangre de Cristo Mountains

Johnson and Bartlett Mesas Including Raton Pass, Northeast
Highlands and Union County. In southeast New Mexico, Chaves County
Plains and Southwest Chaves County.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

merging storm systems will bring a prolonged multi-day period of
showers and thunderstorms producing moderate to heavy rainfall.

high risk of flash flooding.
- Low-lying, poorly drained areas, urban areas and arroyo systems,
and burn scars will be most susceptible. Rivers and streams will
see rises, potentially reaching flood stage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

waves of 4 to 8 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 PM EDT Monday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT this evening. For
the High Rip Current Risk, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Back bay flooding may persist beyond Monday
afternoon.
alerts.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Always obey posted Beach Flags. If you enter the surf zone,
always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 27 at 10:27AM MDT until September 30 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Colorado, including the following areas, Animas
River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, Northwest San Juan
Mountains, Paradox Valley/Lower Dolores River, San Juan River
Basin, Southwest San Juan Mountains and Uncompahgre Plateau and
Dallas Divide and southeast Utah, including the following areas,
Canyonlands/Natural Bridges, La Sal and Abajo Mountains and
Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn scars, at low-water
crossings, and along creeks, streams, washes, arroyos and other
flood-prone locations. Creeks and streams may rise out of their
banks. Unpaved roads could become muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of heavy rainfall, associated with remnant moisture from
Hurricane Polo, are expected to produce numerous showers and
embedded thunderstorms. Heavy rain falling on saturated soils and
burn scars could lead to localized flash flooding and rises on
local rivers.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

alerts.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Plymouth and Bristol
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...From this evening to Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 9.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles for
an extended period of time.  Beware of the dangers of crossing
flooded roadways. The water may be deeper than you think.
Floodwaters have the ability to damage roadways. Heed the advice of
local officials, and evacuate if asked to do so.

- At 10:45 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this evening to a crest of 9.4 feet early tomorrow afternoon. It
will then fall below flood stage Tuesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.4
feet on 03/25/2024.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.

County, Northern Lea and Southern Lea and southwest Texas,
including the following areas, Eastern Culberson, Guadalupe
Mountains Above 7000 Feet, Guadalupe and Delaware Mountains and Van
Horn and Highway 54 Corridor.

* WHEN...From Monday evening through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Tropical moisture from the remnants of Hurricane Polo will
overspread the region, which will promote heavy rain across
southeast New Mexico and far west Texas. Soils in these areas
remain saturated following heavy rains from last week, which will
further promote the risk for flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

AND OAHU THROUGH MONDAY MORNING...

for the Big Island, but continues to produce advisory level surf for

gale-force trades is producing advisory level surf along east
facing shores of Maui, Molokai, Oahu and Kauai. Surf will
diminish below advisory criteria later today for the eastern
islands but will likely continue through tonight for Oahu and
Kauai as Nolo moves westward away from the islands.

diminishing to 7 to 10 ft by this evening.

* WHERE...East facing shores of Molokai, Maui, and the Big
Island.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM HST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 27 at 7:48AM MDT until September 29 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible across
much of central and southern Utah between Monday morning and early
Tuesday morning.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon Country,
Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation
Area/Lake Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper
Sevier River Valleys, Western Canyonlands, Lower Washington County
and Zion National Park.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through early Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn scars
including Cottonwood, Widemouth 2, France Canyon, Monroe Canyon,
Forsyth, and Silver King.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Deep moisture originating from tropical systems in the Eastern
Pacific draws into portions of central and southern Utah on
Monday. Concurrently, an upper-level system traversing the Desert
Southwest will result in ample instability that will produce
widespread heavy rainfall across the area. Isolated heavier
storms will be capable of producing rainfall rates in excess of 1
inch per hour at times.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

alerts.headline: Flood Warning issued September 27 at 9:17AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor remains within Minor Flood Stage and is
actively cresting due to an ongoing period of northerly winds and
tidal effects. River levels are forecast to gradually subside through
Minor Flood Stage this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Sunday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to crest around 2.7 feet today.
The river is then forecast to slowly subside through Minor Flood
Stage this week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 2.6
feet on 10/14/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EDT.
alerts.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 27 at 2:48AM EDT until September 29 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Boston/Norton MA
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Massachusetts, including the following areas,
Barnstable MA, Central Middlesex MA, Dukes MA, Eastern Essex MA,
Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Nantucket MA, Northern
Bristol MA, Northern Middlesex MA, Northern Worcester MA, Southeast
Middlesex MA, Southern Bristol MA, Southern Plymouth MA, Southern
Worcester MA, Suffolk MA, Western Essex MA, Western Norfolk MA and
Western Plymouth MA and Rhode Island, including the following
areas, Block Island RI, Bristol RI, Eastern Kent RI, Newport RI,
Northwest Providence RI, Southeast Providence RI, Washington RI and
Western Kent RI.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of rain will continue across the region right through
Monday. Storm total rainfall amount of 2-4" are expected, but
localized 5-7" amounts are possible. If these higher amounts are
realized...the potential for both urban and small river/stream
flooding would increase. This is particularly true if these
localized higher amounts occur over a vulnerable urban center.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

alerts.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 27 at 2:25AM EDT until September 28 at 3:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf with breaking waves
of 3 to 6 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
alerts.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
alerts.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Sunday, September 27, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Sunday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:

alerts.headline: Flood Watch issued September 26 at 12:01PM MST until September 29 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive and long duration rainfall.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...From Sunday evening through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding will be possible over burn areas, low-water
crossings, creeks, streams, washes and swimming holes. Larger
creeks and rivers may exceed bankfull. Flooding of paved roads and
highway underpasses will be possible. Unpaved roads could become
muddy and impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Low pressure will interact with tropical moisture from the
eastern Pacific. This could potentially produce numerous showers
and embedded thunderstorms, with heavy rain that will fall over
saturated soils and burn scars. This could lead to localized
flash flooding and rises on local rivers, such as the Little
Colorado River.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
alerts.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

alerts.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 25 at 2:21PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
alerts.description:
ESFGJT

In the wake of today's precipitation, our attention will turn to the
Eastern Pacific. Tropical moisture is anticipated to spread across
the Desert Southwest early next week, drawing moisture from a pair of
Hurricanes; Odalys and Polo. The forecast becomes increasing complex
due to a closed low currently forecast to drive across the Southwest
CONUS as Hurricane Polo approaches the Baja California Peninsula.
Strong southerly winds ahead of the low are expected to pull tropical
moisture towards eastern Utah and western Colorado as early as Monday
morning. The challenge and uncertainty in our precipitation forecast
increase as the week progresses and the low traverses our southern
States. Excessive rainfall is most probable over AZ and NM, attm, but
the northerly extent poses a threat to our southern San Juan river
basins. Current forecasts suggests 1 to 3 inches of rain over Monday
morning through Wednesday. At face value, rivers and tributaries will
see a bump up due to said moisture. However, localized heavier
amounts could result in minor flooding across the southern San Juan
foothills and communities further downstream.

Rivers have responded rapidly to recent rainfall due to saturated
soils and increased runoff potential. Thus, prolonged periods of
additional rainfall over these regions would trigger a similar
response. The current precipitation forecast suggests larger peaks in
several creeks and rivers than what has been observed over the
previous 7 days. However, high end probabilistic rainfall amounts
(i.e. above 90th percentile) may lead to rivers exceeding action
stage to minor flooding. Most probable basins to see significant
rises include; the Rio Blanco, San Juan, Piedra, Los Pinos/Vallecito
Creek, and the Animas River Basins.

Convective storms and periods of heavy rainfall fed from said
tropical moisture could result in localized flooding impacts across
the CWA, however, confidence decreases rapidly north of the San
Juans. Please continue to monitor the forecast as these systems
evolve. Especially for those who reside and/or plan to recreate in
the southwest quadrant of the forecast area.
